candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care, printed pp.21-22: Establishing Priorities — prioritize delivery of client care based on acuity; Legal Rights and Responsibilities — recognize limitations of self and others and utilize resources; provide care within legal scope of practice; Referrals — assess need for referral and obtain necessary orders.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — telephone triage prioritization, referral, resources, and scope
candidate.educational_objective: In telephone triage, recognize new chest pressure with shortness of breath as a possible emergency, prioritize EMS evaluation, and act within authorized nursing protocols rather than making a definitive remote diagnosis or independently prescribing treatment.

options.A: Diagnose acute coronary syndrome from the telephone history and give the caller a definitive cardiac diagnosis.
options.B: Perform a focused assessment, recognize a possible emergency, and direct activation of emergency medical services according to protocol and scope.
options.C: Complete a detailed lifetime health history before deciding whether emergency evaluation is needed.
options.D: Recommend a prescription medication for the chest pressure without an authorized order, protocol, or prescriber involvement.

candidate.rationale: NHLBI identifies chest pressure or discomfort and shortness of breath among heart-attack warning symptoms and advises calling 9-1-1 for emergency medical care even when the person is not certain that a heart attack is occurring. The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan requires prioritization based on acuity, use of referrals/resources, and practice within legal scope. Therefore B is the best nursing action: obtain a focused assessment sufficient to recognize the possible emergency and direct EMS activation according to the applicable protocol and scope. A exceeds the available information by making a definitive remote diagnosis, C delays time-sensitive care, and D recommends prescription treatment without an authorized mechanism.
candidate.source_claim_supported: New chest pressure with shortness of breath can represent a time-sensitive cardiac emergency requiring EMS evaluation; the RN should prioritize acuity and referral within scope rather than provide a definitive telephone diagnosis or unauthorized prescription treatment.
